intro: Employed PhD position in limnology at Uppsala University (ref UFV-PA 2026/2846): process-based modelling of phytoplankton succession in lakes. Deadline: 25 November 2026.
description:
About the Position

The Department of Ecology and Genetics, Limnology programme, at Uppsala University advertises a PhD student position in limnology: modelling phytoplankton succession in lakes (reference UFV-PA 2026/2846). The project explores the driving processes behind phytoplankton succession and assesses how phytoplankton will respond to future environmental changes.

Using process-based biogeochemical models, the doctoral student will study how environmental changes - such as climate warming, eutrophication and extreme weather - affect succession patterns in phytoplankton, and identify conditions that favour specific functional groups. The work improves forecasting of phytoplankton communities with direct applications to lake ecosystem function and drinking-water supply.

Duties and Research Focus

  • Data management and process-based, dynamic modelling of lake ecosystems
  • Simulating phytoplankton succession under climate and nutrient scenarios
  • Teaching, coursework and collaboration within the research group
  • The position sits at the intersection of physics, biogeochemistry and ecology, with a strong numerical component

Funding and Employment

Employment and financial support

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
General eligibilityMaster's degree (advanced level) in limnology, aquatic ecology, environmental science, geoscience, biology, environmental technology or another relevant topic; or 240 higher-education credits including 60 advanced with an independent thesis; or equivalent knowledge. Candidates not yet graduated but expected to meet requirements by the access date may apply.
Numerical skillsDocumented skills with advanced numerical methods (modelling, statistics or large-scale data analysis); programming experience, for example in R or Python, is required.
MeritsPrevious experience with lake models or other process-based models, familiarity with lake processes such as stratification and aquatic biogeochemical cycles, and a good understanding of phytoplankton ecology.
EnglishMust be able to express themselves very well in both oral and written English.

Application dates

Recruitment information

How to Apply

Apply through Uppsala University's recruitment system via the official link by 25 November 2026. The application should contain a personal letter (maximum 2 pages) describing your research interests and suitability, a CV, a brief description of your education, degree certificates and transcripts including your master's thesis, and contact details for at least two references. Contact: Jorrit Mesman, jorrit.mesman@ebc.uu.se.

About the Host Department

The Department of Ecology and Genetics at Uppsala University hosts the Limnology programme within the Evolutionary Biology Centre (EBC), one of Europe's leading environments for evolutionary biology and ecology research.

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

  • Application deadline: 25 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
